thesis: Two free commanders that tax every card that moves — Brallin charges 1 damage to each opponent per DISCARD, Shabraz charges a +1/+1 counter per DRAW — sitting behind seventeen wheels, so that emptying and refilling a hand bills the table twice for the same seven cards.

stages.label: THE 42 SOURCES
stages.what_it_does: Pays for the wheels and, more importantly, for the commanders — the machine does not start when a wheel is drawn, it starts when a tax collector is on the battlefield. deck-facts/deck-audit: 36 lands, 42 mana sources (target >= 39), 2 taplands (target <= 8), and 9 ramp copies against a 10-12 target. colour-sources is one of five axes UNDER target (with ramp, interaction, protection and interaction-breadth), at -6 sources on the worst colour — this is a WUR deck whose two commanders cost {3}{W}{U} and {3}{R} and whose kill piece Niv-Mizzet, Parun costs {U}{U}{U}{R}{R}{R}. The goldfish reads 4.004 mana on turn 4 and 5.455 on turn 6 (10,000 games, seed 42), which is why Brallin lands at mean turn 4.276 and Shabraz at 5.391. Five of the six accelerants make or use Treasure, and `model_treasures` is deliberately OFF per `_flags_note`, so none of Smothering Tithe, Generous Plunderer, Treasure Map // Treasure Cove or Sticky Fingers is priced in any figure here; Generous Plunderer is the one card model-coverage calls DARK on that channel. Sticky Fingers is an Aura that produces only after its creature connects, so it is the weakest member of a stage that is already under target.

evidence.note: 22 of the 36 lands; city-6 holds the other 14 and city-4 the six accelerants
the map split one landbase into two cities; nothing functional separates them
the Ramp city also holds Currency Converter and Sorcerer Class, which this model reads as conversion and fodder respectively
deck-audit ramp 9 copies against a 10-12 target

stages.label: THE WHEEL — THE ONLY THING THAT EMPTIES A HAND
stages.what_it_does: Every payoff in this deck is a tax collector with nothing to tax until a hand empties and refills, and `_required_note` marks this the ONE required group. It is not the scarce part: 17 cards is 74.5% of an opening seven, assembled 98.2% of games at mean turn 1.709, 94.2% by turn 6. The scarce part is downstream — the partner who charges the tax arrives at mean turn 4.276. A wheel cast before Brallin is a redraw, not a payment. The group also splits three ways on what it actually does, and only one third pays. Six DISCARD (Jace's Archivist, Magus of the Wheel, Reforge the Soul, Tolarian Winds, Wheel of Fortune, Windfall) — that subgroup is 36.4% of an opener and assembles 82.9%, 67.4% by turn 6. Six SHUFFLE the hand into the library and two bottom it; `_shuffle_note` prices the difference at 4,000 games, seed 3: rewriting the six shufflers to discard leaves card draw identical at 14.78 extra cards by turn ten while cards discarded moves 7.58 -> 12.22 and per-opponent ping damage 9.61 -> 14.53. They refill as well and pay half as much. Three more (Burning Inquiry, Khorvath's Fury, Wheel of Misfortune) discard by oracle text but carry no `discard` channel in model-coverage, so no figure here credits them.

evidence.note: 15 of 17; Arjun and Whirlpool Warrior sit in city-0 because they are creatures
modal role draw:burst; deck-audit prices the group at 74.5% of an opener

stages.label: THE HAND IS THE FUEL — AND THESE ARE THE MOUTHS
stages.what_it_does: What this engine converts is its own hand, so a discard is not a cost here, it is the payment. These nine let the deck pay between wheels: Faithless Looting, Artist's Talent and Sorcerer Class loot (each loot is one Brallin ping AND one Shabraz counter); Ceremonial Knife, Mindless Automaton and Jaxis, the Troublemaker are activated outlets that discard on demand; Astral Drift and Curator of Mysteries are cyclers that turn a dead card into the same two payments. Library of Leng belongs here rather than with hand size: its replacement puts a discarded card on TOP of the library instead of the graveyard, which makes every payment free, and whether the event is still a discard for Brallin is the single most load-bearing unsettled rules question in the deck (open_questions). The measured floor is 7.784 cards discarded by turn ten (10,000 games, seed 42), and three of these nine are outside it: model-coverage lists Artist's Talent and Astral Drift `invisible`, and reads Library of Leng on the `target` channel only. That makes 7.784 a floor on the discard side, not an estimate.

evidence.note: four of nine; the other five scatter across city-2, city-3, city-4 and city-5
the declared group 'A discard converted to board or cards' assembles 93.9%

stages.label: THE DRAWS THAT ARE NOT WHEELS
stages.what_it_does: Shabraz taxes EVERY draw, not only a wheel's, so a steady draw is a steady stream of +1/+1 counters and life, and — with a wincon piece out — of damage. These five draw without emptying the hand: Rhystic Study and Mind's Eye tax the opponents' turns, Nezahal draws on each opposing noncreature spell, Kefnet the Mindful is a {3}{U} draw outlet on an indestructible flier, and Enduring Curiosity draws on each creature's combat damage. Two things the reader must not mis-read. First, the measured 14.946 extra cards by turn ten (10,000 games, seed 42) does NOT include Rhystic Study or Mind's Eye — model-coverage lists both `invisible`, and goldfish_metrics `card_advantage` models 4 of the 35 cards that draw. Second, Kefnet's hand-size clause runs the other way from the group it is declared in: it REQUIRES seven cards in hand to attack, so it is a big-hand payoff, not hand-size relief (see proposed_goldfish_edits). Enduring Curiosity's draws are combat-gated and the goldfish has no blockers, so its contribution is not evidence.

evidence.note: Mind's Eye, Rhystic Study, Enduring Curiosity and Kefnet sit in city-2; Nezahal in city-5 with the wheels

stages.label: THE TWO TAX COLLECTORS, AND THE FOUR CLERKS
stages.what_it_does: This is the engine proper and both halves of it are free in the command zone, which is the deck's real advantage. Brallin turns each DISCARD into a +1/+1 counter and 1 damage to EACH opponent; Shabraz turns each DRAW into a +1/+1 counter and 1 life. A wheel therefore pays twice, once on the way out and once on the way back. Brallin is cast by turn 6 in 92.4% of games at mean turn 4.276; Shabraz by turn 6 in 81.8% at mean turn 5.391 (10,000 games, seed 42). Brallin is the single point of failure not because he is scarce — he is a commander — but because every damage figure in this model is his trigger, and the deck holds exactly two cards that grant him shroud or hexproof (Lightning Greaves, Swiftfoot Boots, 13.7% of an opener, assembled 56.8%). The four clerks convert the same events into something other than damage: Rielle turns the first discard each turn into that many cards, Containment Construct and Currency Converter recover discarded cards from the graveyard, Drake Haven turns a discard into a 2/2 flier for {1}. Every card in this stage reads 'whenever you draw' or 'whenever you discard' — which is exactly why the map cannot see the stage at all.

evidence.note: holds both commanders, but also Stromkirk Noble and Marketback Walker, which this model leaves unassigned
Rielle, Containment Construct and Drake Haven address here as bodies/permanents
engine-facts scatter: this declared group spreads over four cities and is the deck's least map-visible component

stages.label: THE AIR FORCE THE COMMANDERS FLY WITH
stages.what_it_does: The second declared route. Both commanders fly and both grow on every card that moves, so a wheel that is not lethal on the ping half is still a large evasive board: mean board power reaches 9.501 on turn 6 and 17.517 on turn 10, from 2.342 and 6.697 bodies (10,000 games, seed 42). Chasm Skulker, Shark Typhoon, The Locust God, Ominous Seas, Improbable Alliance and Vanguard Suppressor each turn a draw into a body or a counter, and four of them make FLYING bodies. The declared per-draw BOARD group is 36.4% of an opener and assembles 90.2%; the AIR KILL pair assembles 78.2%, 52.7% by turn 6. THE STANDING WARNING APPLIES TO THIS WHOLE STAGE: the goldfish has no blockers, so its combat figures — kill-by-turn-10 0.976, mean kill turn 7.285 — are not evidence about this route, and the CLAUDE.md record is explicit that a go-wide token verdict from a goldfish has been wrong before by 29.07 -> 18.20 damage in Forge. Read the ping figure instead: 9.936 cumulative per-opponent damage by turn ten is non-combat and unblockable, and it is the only damage number here that a blocker cannot answer.

evidence.note: three of six; Ominous Seas and Shark Typhoon are in city-0, Chasm Skulker in city-3
deck-audit threat-density 8 copies against a >= 3 target

stages.label: TWO PAIRS OF BOOTS AND THREE ANSWERS
stages.what_it_does: The whole machine is a 4-drop and a 5-drop, and deck-audit puts protection UNDER target at 3 copies against 5-7, interaction UNDER at 7 against >= 8, and interaction-breadth UNDER at 2 answered classes against >= 5, with enchantment, graveyard and land named as classes with no answer detected. Lightning Greaves and Swiftfoot Boots are the only cards that keep Brallin on the table through a removal spell: 13.7% of an opener, assembled 56.8%, 34.9% by turn 6, mean turn 5.065 — which is after Brallin's own mean arrival of 4.276, so the protection usually shows up late. Decree of Silence, Nimble Obstructionist and Elesh Norn // The Argent Etchings answer opposing plays rather than protect ours, and two of the three do it by CYCLING, which is itself a discard and therefore also a payment. One card the taxonomy missed, per deck-audit's own note: Talon Gates of Madara can phase a creature out, which is protection the count does not include. The declared answer group also names Commit // Memory, which this model files under ignition because its Memory half is a wheel.

evidence.note: four of five; Commit // Memory, the fifth declared answer, is in city-5 and is modelled as ignition here
deck-audit: protection 3 copies against a 5-7 target, UNDER

stages.label: THE PER-CARD BURN THAT STACKS ON BRALLIN
stages.what_it_does: Brallin alone makes a seven-card wheel 7 to each opponent. These four stack a SECOND payment onto the same cards, and the declared arithmetic is one wheel at 7, plus Glint-Horn Buccaneer for 14, plus Psychosis Crawler on the redraw for 21 — two wheels closing a 40-life table. The claim is untested: this deck has ZERO checker-passed stacks, so every line here is filed in open_questions with settled_by resolve-stack, and `verified_by` is null throughout. The split matters. Enumerating every card in the 99 that triggers on a discard — Brallin, Containment Construct, Currency Converter, Curator of Mysteries, Drake Haven, Glint-Horn Buccaneer and Rielle — Glint-Horn Buccaneer is the only one that deals DAMAGE — one card, 7.1% of an opening seven, assembled 34.7%, 18.1% by turn 6, mean turn 5.652, and deck-audit names it the deck's one priced single point of failure. The other three pay on a DRAW: Psychosis Crawler drains 1 per draw, Niv-Mizzet, Parun pings 1 per draw, Irencrag Pyromancer deals 3 on the second draw each turn. That group is 19.9% of an opener and assembles 70.0%. THE WHEEL KILL as declared — a discard wheel plus any of the four — assembles 67.1%, 37.9% by turn 6, mean turn 5.661. The trustworthy measurement is 9.936 cumulative per-opponent ping damage by turn ten, because it is non-combat and no blocker touches it.

evidence.note: Niv-Mizzet and Psychosis Crawler address as 'Finishers'; Glint-Horn and Irencrag sit in city-0 as bodies, so the kill has two addresses
deck-audit: 1 declared target rests on a one-card component, 7.1% of an opener

lines.note: CLAIM. Wheel of Fortune is {2}{R}; the goldfish reads 3.160 mana on turn 3 (10,000 games, seed 42), and the ignition group assembles at mean turn 1.709 — the mana is never the constraint on starting.

CLAIM, the deck's whole thesis: a seven-card hand discarded to a wheel is seven separate Brallin triggers, 7 damage to EACH opponent and seven +1/+1 counters. Unverified — no stack has passed for this deck.

CLAIM, the second half of the same wheel: seven draws is seven Shabraz triggers, seven counters and 7 life. Whether one wheel pays both commanders in one resolution is exactly what a stack has to settle.
CLAIM. Both read 'whenever you discard a card', so the declared doubling to 14 is two independent triggers per card. This is the line the single point of failure sits on.
CLAIM. The redraw half: Psychosis Crawler drains 1 per card drawn, so the declared third increment to 21. Crawler is also a wheel-sized body, since its power equals hand size.

CLAIM. The between-wheels payment: a loot is two draws and two discards, so two pings and four counters across the pair of commanders. 7.784 cards discarded by turn ten is the measured floor on this channel.
CLAIM. An activated outlet turns spare mana into pings at will rather than waiting for a wheel; Glint-Horn's own {1}{R} outlet only works while it is attacking, which the goldfish cannot model.
CLAIM. Shabraz taxes draws on any turn, so opponent-triggered draw is engine fuel. model-coverage lists Rhystic Study `invisible`, so no figure in this brief includes it.
CLAIM, the air route: a wheel under The Locust God is one 1/1 flying haste Insect per card drawn. Board figures from the goldfish are NOT evidence for this line — it has no blockers.
CLAIM. Greaves is the cheapest answer to the deck's one real failure mode, Brallin dying; the protection group assembles at mean turn 5.065 against Brallin's 4.276, so it is usually late.

map_disagreements.why: The declared group 'A discard converted to board or cards' spreads over FOUR cities, the widest scatter in the deck. The reason is that 'whenever you discard' is not what these cards are ABOUT in their own text: Currency Converter reads as a Treasure maker and addresses in Ramp, Drake Haven and Containment Construct read as permanents and address in Bodies, Mindless Automaton reads as a counters creature and addresses in Payoffs. The trigger they share is one clause each. This is the part of the engine a reader cannot see from card text, and it is where the deck's value actually comes from.

engine-facts scatter: the damage half of the declared kill sits 2 in Bodies and 2 in Finishers. Niv-Mizzet, Parun and Psychosis Crawler are written as marquee payoffs and cluster together; Glint-Horn Buccaneer and Irencrag Pyromancer are small red creatures whose text happens to say 'deals damage', so they cluster with the other bodies. The map is reading rarity and shape; the engine reads the trigger.

This stage is the engine's own invention and has NO address: nine cards across five of the deck's seven cities. Nothing in the text of Ceremonial Knife, Astral Drift, Sorcerer Class and Faithless Looting looks alike — an Equipment, a cycling enchantment, a Class and a red sorcery. What unites them is that each converts a card in hand into two commander triggers, which is a fact about THIS deck's commanders and appears in no card's text.

15 of 17 cluster cleanly — the tightest agreement in the deck. The two exceptions are Arjun, the Shifting Flame and Whirlpool Warrior, which address as creatures because they are creatures. The map has no way to know that a body whose text wheels is a wheel.

The map split one 36-land base into two cities (22 and 14) with nothing functional separating them, and filed the six accelerants in a third. The split is a property of the projection, not of the deck.

unassigned.why: The deck's only tutor, and it cannot reach the engine. It searches an ARTIFACT to the graveyard and returns artifacts of mana value 3 or less. Enumerating the 14 artifacts in the 99: in range are Arcane Signet, Ceremonial Knife, Containment Construct, Currency Converter, Library of Leng, Lightning Greaves, Marketback Walker, Sol Ring, Swiftfoot Boots and Treasure Map // Treasure Cove; out of range are Mindless Automaton (4), Teferi's Puzzle Box (4), Mind's Eye (5) and Psychosis Crawler (5). No wheel is an artifact, so it cannot find ignition, and the one artifact that closes a game (Psychosis Crawler) is above its cap. model-coverage reads it as DARK on the sacrifice channel, which is off.

A one-drop that grows only on its own combat damage. It has no draw trigger, no discard trigger, and puts no counter on anything the commanders care about, so no card movement touches it. goldfish_metrics `combat_effects_not_modelled` names it, so it contributes nothing to any figure in this brief either.

Surveil on creature ETB, then unblockability and a blink at higher levels. Surveil is not a draw and not a discard, so it pays neither commander. model-coverage lists it `invisible`: no channel reads it. `combat_effects_not_modelled` names it as well.

Unblockable, with a combat-damage mode chart whose draw mode can be chosen once. One draw across a game is one +1/+1 counter on Shabraz; it neither discards nor triggers on card movement, and the counters it makes stay on itself.

An {X}{X} body that pays cards only when it DIES, which is a mode this engine never chooses on purpose — there is no sacrifice outlet (model_sacrifice is off, and `_flags_note` says the two DARK cards are not a sacrifice engine). Until it dies it is a vanilla creature that no wheel, discard or draw interacts with.

Draws nothing until a FOURTH combat-damage trigger has put a fourth quest counter on it. The goldfish has no blockers, so even its optimistic reading is unearned here, and model-coverage lists the card `invisible` — no channel reads it at all.

open_questions.question: Does one Wheel of Fortune with Brallin, Skyshark Rider on the battlefield trigger Brallin once per card discarded — seven triggers, 7 damage to each opponent and seven +1/+1 counters — and does the same wheel then trigger Shabraz seven times on the redraw?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the deck's entire declared thesis and the arithmetic in goldfish_targets `note`. Nothing in this deck has ever been checked: zero passing stacks. If the discard of a hand is a single event rather than seven, every damage figure in the declaration is wrong by a factor of seven.

open_questions.question: With Brallin and Glint-Horn Buccaneer both on the battlefield, does a seven-card wheel deal 14 to each opponent — two independent triggers per discarded card — and does adding Psychosis Crawler on the redraw reach the declared 21?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The declared kill. Glint-Horn Buccaneer is the deck's one priced single point of failure (one card, 7.1% of an opener, assembled 34.7%), so the value of holding it rests entirely on this doubling being real.

open_questions.question: If Library of Leng replaces a discard by putting the card on top of the library instead of into the graveyard, does Brallin still trigger, and do Rielle, Containment Construct and Currency Converter still see the event?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Library of Leng would make every payment free, which changes the deck from one that spends cards to one that does not. If the replacement stops the trigger, the card is close to a blank and its slot is the cheapest improvement in the 99. model-coverage reads it on the `target` channel only, so no measurement here answers it.

open_questions.question: Can Jace's Archivist be activated every turn for {U} and a tap to wheel the table, and does Brallin trigger for the pilot's own discarded hand each time, including when the pilot's hand is smaller than the largest hand discarded?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The simulator learned to read activated wheels only today, and Jace's Archivist is the only repeatable one in the deck (Magus of the Wheel and Whirlpool Warrior sacrifice themselves). A repeatable wheel changes the deck from a burst engine to a recurring one, and every ignition figure above was measured with that new reading.

open_questions.question: Does Niv-Mizzet, Parun's per-draw ping trigger on each of the seven cards a wheel draws, and may each ping be aimed at a different target?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Niv-Mizzet, Parun and Irencrag Pyromancer are the two wincon pieces whose damage reads 'any target' and can therefore be aimed at CREATURES; Glint-Horn Buccaneer hits each opponent and Psychosis Crawler drains life, so neither can. That matters because deck-audit has interaction-breadth UNDER target at 2 answered classes against >= 5, and a wheel under Niv-Mizzet is the deck's only repeatable source of creature removal.

open_questions.question: Does Glint-Horn Buccaneer's {1}{R}, Discard a card: Draw a card loop with Brallin into a repeatable ping while it is attacking, and what stops it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the loop is mana-limited rather than card-limited it is a second kill route that needs no wheel at all, which would change what the ignition stage is for. The activation is attack-gated and the goldfish has no blockers, so the simulator cannot answer it.

open_questions.question: Does the simulator read Burning Inquiry, Khorvath's Fury and Wheel of Misfortune as hand-refill effects and as discards? model-coverage lists all three with a `target` channel and NO `discard` channel, while Wheel of Fortune, Windfall and Tolarian Winds carry `discard`.
open_questions.why_it_matters: All three discard by oracle text, and the declaration counts them in the 17-card ignition group but not in the six-card DISCARD group. If the model cannot see them, the measured 7.784 cards discarded and 9.936 per-opponent damage by turn ten are floors that omit three of the deck's nine oracle-text discard wheels.

open_questions.question: How much of the deck's discard and ping output comes from cards model-coverage calls `invisible` — Artist's Talent, Astral Drift, Gossip's Talent, Mind's Eye, Rhystic Study and Waterbender Ascension — plus the DARK treasure and sacrifice channels?
open_questions.why_it_matters: goldfish_metrics `card_advantage` models 4 of the 35 cards in this deck that draw. Every figure in this engine model is therefore a floor, and the reader needs to know by how much before treating 14.946 extra cards by turn ten as the deck's card advantage.

open_questions.question: Is the wheel or the commander the real ignition? The wheel group assembles 98.2% at mean turn 1.709, while Brallin arrives at mean turn 4.276 and Shabraz at 5.391.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The declaration calls the wheel the ignition and marks it `required`. The measured turns say the binding constraint is the commander, not the wheel — so a figure like 'assembled 98.2%' describes the abundant half of the window. A group requiring a wheel AND a live commander would price the real first window, and would change what every downstream reader treats as this deck's ignition.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: A DISCARD wheel drawn — the half that pays Brallin (the other eight shuffle or bottom)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Either add Burning Inquiry, Khorvath's Fury and Wheel of Misfortune to the any_of (taking it from 6 cards to 9), or rename the group to say explicitly that it is scoped to the six the SIMULATOR reads as discards. Resolve the goldfish question first; do not do both.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: All three discard by oracle text — Burning Inquiry 'discards three cards at random', Khorvath's Fury 'each friend discards all cards from their hand', Wheel of Misfortune 'each player who didn't choose the lowest number discards their hand'. The label's arithmetic (6 discard + 8 shuffle-or-bottom = 14) is the MODEL'S set, not the deck's, and a reader who counts wheels in the 99 finds 17. As written the group understates the deck's real discard density by three cards, and THE WHEEL KILL's first clause inherits the same understatement.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Hand-size relief drawn — the deck routinely holds more than seven
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Remove Kefnet the Mindful and add Reliquary Tower, leaving Library of Leng, Nezahal, Primal Tide and Reliquary Tower.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Enumerating every card in the 99 whose text says 'You have no maximum hand size': Library of Leng, Nezahal, Primal Tide and Reliquary Tower — three cards, and the group names only two of them. Kefnet the Mindful has no such clause; it reads 'can't attack or block unless you have seven or more cards in hand', which is a big-hand PAYOFF and runs the opposite way. The group as written measures a mix of two different jobs.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Ramp drawn — an accelerant of any kind
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Split or annotate: Sticky Fingers and Generous Plunderer produce only after combat damage or an upkeep the model does not read, so they are not accelerants on the same terms as Sol Ring and Arcane Signet.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The group measures 93.5% assembled at mean turn 3.386, and deck-audit still reports ramp UNDER target at 9 copies against 10-12. Both figures are true and they describe different things: five of the seven members make or use Treasure and `model_treasures` is OFF by deliberate choice (`_flags_note`), so the 93.5% is a rate of DRAWING cards whose effect is not modelled. A reader will take it as a rate of having mana.
